note: The National Bank of Georgia's Order 195/04 (the rule on providing information to a credit information bureau, as amended to 2025), point 11: five years after a credit is repaid, its information is available to lenders only without the person's identifying data, written as five years. No source read states how many days after its due date a missed payment is reported, so the days are the game's reading: the bureau's next monthly update.

sources.title: National Bank of Georgia, Order №195/04 (English)
sources.said: If 5 (five) years have passed since the repayment of a credit/loan, off-balance sheet liability (letter of credit, guarantee, etc.), or other type of financial obligation, information about this obligation should be available to lending organizations and information recipients/providers without the identifying data of the data subject.
